entry.title: russh: Agent server never calls `Agent::confirm`, so keys added with the confirm constraint (`ssh-add -c`) sign without confirmation
entry.summary:
HIGH 4.3 · GHSA — rust · score 0.500 · ×3 reports · CVE-2026-116696, CVE-2026-116773, CVE-2026-116794

Affected: russh. ### Summary The agent server in `russh::keys::agent::server` never calls `Agent::confirm` before signing with a key that was added with the confirm constraint. That constraint is `SSH_AGENT_CONSTRAIN_CONFIRM` (RFC 9987 §5.2.7.2), which is what `ssh-add -c` sends. The call was replaced by a hard-coded `true` in 3e04597 ("Native async traits encore", #455), first released in 0.50.0-beta.12. Every release since, up to and including 0.64.1, signs requests for confirm-constrained keys without asking the `Agent` implementation. A user who added a key with `-c` is therefore never asked to confirm.

entry.title: graphql-scalars PhoneNumber scalar is vulnerable to regular expression denial of service
entry.summary:
HIGH 7.5 · GHSA — npm · score 0.188 · CVE-2026-115887

Affected: graphql-scalars. ## Summary The regular expression behind `GraphQLPhoneNumber` since 1.24.1 backtracks exponentially. A string made of a run of digits followed by one character that makes the match fail (for example `"1".repeat(30) + "x"`) blocks the JavaScript thread for seconds, and every additional digit doubles the time. graphql-js calls `parseLiteral` while *validating* a document and `parseValue` while coercing variables, so the regex runs for every request that merely contains such a value in a `PhoneNumber` position, before execution and before any authentication or authorization step of the server.
